properties.name: Blue Ridge
properties.summary: Mountainous northeast Georgia with high elevations and major headwater areas.
properties.why: Elevation and terrain influence rainfall, streams, recreation, road routes, and settlement.

properties.name: Ridge and Valley
properties.summary: Long ridges and valleys across northwest Georgia.
properties.why: Parallel landforms shape transportation corridors, farming areas, and community locations.

properties.name: Appalachian Plateau
properties.summary: Georgia’s smallest physiographic region in the far northwest.
properties.why: Plateau terrain connects Georgia to the broader Appalachian landscape and helps explain regional geology.

properties.name: Piedmont
properties.summary: Rolling uplands across central and north-central Georgia, including metro Atlanta.
properties.why: Population, roads, water demand, industry, and the Fall Line all connect strongly to Piedmont geography.

properties.name: Coastal Plain
properties.summary: Broad lower-elevation region extending across southern Georgia to the Atlantic coast.
properties.why: Flatter terrain supports major agriculture, wetlands, long river reaches, highways, and coastal trade.

properties.name: Brasstown Bald
properties.summary: Georgia’s highest natural point.
properties.why: Mountain elevation influences drainage, ecosystems, recreation, and transportation routes.

properties.name: Blood Mountain
properties.summary: A prominent Blue Ridge summit on the Appalachian Trail.
properties.why: Mountain elevation influences drainage, ecosystems, recreation, and transportation routes.

properties.name: Lookout Mountain
properties.summary: A plateau/ridge landmark overlooking northwest Georgia.
properties.why: Mountain elevation influences drainage, ecosystems, recreation, and transportation routes.

properties.name: Chattahoochee River
properties.summary: Major river flowing from north Georgia past the Atlanta region and along the western state boundary.
properties.why: It connects headwaters, reservoirs, drinking-water supply, recreation, hydropower, cities, and downstream communities.

properties.name: Savannah River
properties.summary: Major eastern boundary river reaching the Atlantic at Savannah.
properties.why: The river connects water resources, interstate geography, ecosystems, industry, and maritime trade.

properties.name: Flint River
properties.summary: River beginning near metro Atlanta and flowing south through western Georgia.
properties.why: Its basin links urban headwaters, agriculture, water supply, ecology, and downstream water management.

properties.name: Ocmulgee River
properties.summary: Central Georgia river flowing through the Macon area toward the Altamaha system.
properties.why: It illustrates how central Georgia cities and watersheds connect toward the coast.

properties.name: Lake Lanier
properties.summary: Large reservoir on the upper Chattahoochee system.
properties.why: Reservoirs connect flood control, water supply, hydropower, recreation, ecosystems, and population growth.

properties.name: I-75 corridor
properties.summary: Major north–south interstate corridor through Macon and Atlanta.
properties.why: It connects freight, commuters, industries, cities, and interstate commerce.

properties.name: I-85 corridor
properties.summary: Major interstate from west Georgia through Atlanta toward the northeast.
properties.why: It is a major passenger and freight route and helps explain development patterns around interchanges.

properties.name: I-20 corridor
properties.summary: East–west interstate crossing Georgia through metro Atlanta and Augusta.
properties.why: East–west connectivity links urban centers, warehouses, industries, and neighboring states.

properties.name: I-16 corridor
properties.summary: Interstate connecting Macon with Savannah.
properties.why: This corridor is especially important for inland movement of cargo associated with the Port of Savannah.

properties.name: Atlanta–Savannah rail corridor
properties.summary: Simplified educational representation of a major inland freight connection.
properties.why: Rail moves high volumes of freight and complements highway and port infrastructure.

properties.name: Atlanta
properties.summary: State capital and major transportation/economic center.
properties.why: Cities are nodes where population, transportation, water systems, government, and economic activity meet.

properties.name: Savannah
properties.summary: Historic coastal city and major port center.
properties.why: Cities are nodes where population, transportation, water systems, government, and economic activity meet.

properties.name: Augusta
properties.summary: Eastern Georgia city on the Savannah River.
properties.why: Cities are nodes where population, transportation, water systems, government, and economic activity meet.

properties.name: Macon
properties.summary: Central Georgia city near the Ocmulgee River and major transport corridors.
properties.why: Cities are nodes where population, transportation, water systems, government, and economic activity meet.

properties.name: Columbus
properties.summary: West Georgia city on the Chattahoochee River.
properties.why: Cities are nodes where population, transportation, water systems, government, and economic activity meet.

properties.name: Port of Savannah
properties.summary: Major maritime freight gateway on the Georgia coast.
properties.why: Ports connect Georgia businesses to national and international trade through ships, rail, roads, and warehouses.

properties.name: Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport
properties.summary: Major passenger and cargo airport south of downtown Atlanta.
properties.why: Air transportation links Georgia quickly to national and global networks.

properties.name: Buford Dam
properties.summary: Dam at Lake Lanier on the Chattahoochee River system.
properties.why: Dams can combine water storage, hydropower, flood management, recreation, and downstream-flow effects.

properties.name: Garden City Terminal study area
properties.summary: Port-side logistics study point near Savannah.
properties.why: Terminals demonstrate how ships, cranes, containers, rail, trucks, warehouses, and highways operate as one system.
